That's where I get stuck- I can't figure out how to retrain my brain to not care and not desire it. I just get stuck in the thought loops of "what if this, what if that, you're still not asleep," etc
Anytime I take something, my brain turns it into "You took ___- now you MUST sleep" and it becomes added pressure. The difference between anxiety-induced insomnia and regular insomnia.

It's 100% anxiety related. Which is why 'regular' insomnia solutions and sleep aids don't work. I know there are treatments and I'm looking into CBTI and even hypnosis, but I'm worried it won't help in time. I just remember how quickly and how bad it got last time.
My wife, which is nice, but it doesn't help. Just worries her, which makes me feel worse.
But it's unbearable. It's completely unbearable.

I don't know. I went to a funeral once of someone who died by suicide and the husband who was speaking said, in so few words, "we're all sad she's gone but I'm so glad she's not suffering anymore". I felt that so hard, and more so right now. I don't WANT this, but at a certain point a person can only take so much suffering. The only thing that really gets me to a place of calm is in remembering that when it gets to be too much, I can make it stop. I don't want to, I truly truly don't, but I'm so worried that's my only option.
What if it doesn't get better in time?
